Let me see if I understand.

Every mass has a gravitational pull, which can be displayed as a vector and a magnitude. You're trying to find out how to calculate between multiple masses of objects which are in each other's gravitational pull?

The basic equation for gravitational pull is

F = (GMm)/R^2

F is the force of attraction between two objects in newtons (N) G is the Universal Gravitational Constant = 6.674*10^−11 N-m^2/kg^2 M and m are the masses of the two objects in kilograms (kg) R is the separation in meters (m) between the objects, as measured from their centers of mass

However, all Forces are a vector to begin with, since a force is always acting upon an object at a certain direction. So, in order to write a vector from the force, you need to look at the angle at which the force is being applied and separate it (assuming 2D) along the y and x axis which you would break up into component form of Fcos(theta) and Fsin(Theta).

Using the formula for an angle between two vectors, cos(theta) = (A dot B) / (abs(A) abs(B)), you can find the various angles as well. Where A and B are vectors.
